stemMd: In the Brønsted–Lowry description, what does a base do?
explanationMd: A Brønsted–Lowry acid donates a proton and a base accepts one. The definition is broader than substances containing hydroxide ions; ammonia, for example, can accept a proton to form ammonium. No nuclear particle other than the transferred proton is exchanged.

distractorRationale.a: Proton donation defines an acid in this description.
distractorRationale.d: Acid-base reactions do not involve neutron transfer.
distractorRationale.c: Ammonia is a base without a metal atom.
distractorRationale.e: Solubility does not define a Brønsted–Lowry base.
